summary: Theodor Mommsen was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the Christianeum and Kiel University. He held academic posts at Leipzig, Zurich, Breslau, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and Frederick William University Berlin.

Theodor Nöldeke specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. After studying under Theodor Benfey and Heinrich Ewald and attending Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin, he held posts at Göttingen, Kiel University, and the University of Strasbourg.
Theodor Schultze was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied law at Kiel University from around 1843 to 1847 and also studied at Frederick William University Berlin.

Theodor Zachariae worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Leipzig, Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Hermann Sauppe, and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller. He subsequently held academic appointments at the University of Greifswald and the University of Halle.
Theodor von Oppolzer studied at the University of Vienna from around 1859 to 1865 and later held a post there from circa 1866 until 1886.

Theodore Dwight Woolsey studied at Hopkins School, Yale, and Princeton. Working in linguistics and other fields, he served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and president of the American Oriental Society from around 1868 to 1881.

Theodore Riccardi worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Columbia University, attested in 1974–1976 and 1990, and served as guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society, attested in 1989.
Theodore Riccardi Jr. is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics who served as a faculty member (attested 2014) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2026) at Columbia University.

Theodore Stcherbatsky was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He served as a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences, attested between 1927 and 1931.
Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen was a scholar of religious studies and other fields who held academic posts at the University of Groningen from 1941 to 1956 and at Utrecht University from 1956 to 1969.

Theodorus Willem Juynboll studied at Leiden University from circa 1884 to 1893 under Hendrik Arent Hamaker. Working in linguistics, religious studies, and other fields, he held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.

Theofil Simenschy was an Indologist and linguist who studied and earned his PhD at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University. He spent his career there as an assistant, docent, and Professor of Classical Languages and Comparative Indo-European Philology.

Theophil Gubler worked in Indology and linguistics, completing his Ph.D. at the University of Basel under Jacob Wackernagel by 1903. He later served as a teacher at the Gymnasium am Münsterplatz from 1906 to 1934.

Theos Bernard worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned degrees at the University of Arizona and completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at Columbia University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Herbert Schneider.

Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Chicago, attested in 2019, and a Vertretungsprofessor post at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, attested in 2026.

Thich Nhat Hanh was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied in Vietnam and at Columbia, Princeton, and Princeton Theological Seminary. He held teaching posts at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh University, and Cornell.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under the supervision of Shalini Singhal, attested in 2012.

Thierry Mathou studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po. Working in Tibetology and other fields, he held an appointment as an associated political scientist at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Thierry Meynard is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who earned his PhD at Peking University under Yulie Lou. He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University around 2006 and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies in 2012.

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West, attested in 2007, studying under Lewis Lancaster, Ananda Guruge, and doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya.
